writeup: TIC 468122704 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 8.6546 days. The TESS mission detected a primary eclipse with a depth of 22.26 percent dimming, producing a strong automated signal with a detection significance of 488.4. Pixel-level analysis confirmed this signature, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 24.0, though the centroid offset of 3.6 arcsec from the target warrants attention. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be previously unknown. The pipeline's machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.44, indicating moderate confidence in its status as a genuine target. No data quality issues were identified during automated checks.
